title: FAKE EXAMPLE — Which Atari game was this network trained on?
summary:
**This is fake data for layout testing.** Opus 5.5 named the correct game in *12 of 15* scored attempts (numbers invented).

Controls: on random-init networks it declined to name a game in 5 of 5 attempts. See `logs/_example/` and [the original post](https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/).

runs.label: Breakout · attempt 1
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
FAKE: Byte 72 has unusually large, sign-structured outgoing weights into units 3, 6 and 11 — the kind of pattern you'd expect for a horizontal position the policy tracks closely.
FAKE: The output layer differentiates two actions (indices 3 and 4) far more than the rest, consistent with a left/right paddle.
FAKE: Bias b3 is nearly uniform, so action preference is driven by inputs rather than a fixed habit.
FAKE: Taken together: a game with a single horizontally moving paddle and a ball whose position is in RAM — most likely Breakout.
